name: beam-eval-v1

judge.calls: one per answer; every rubric item of the question graded in that call

primary.aggregation: each question scores the mean of its own rubric items; each conversation scores the mean of its questions; the arm scores the mean over conversations
primary.reason: The primary answers one clear question: can the system keep, retrieve and correctly use the facts a question needs? The seven fact abilities name a fact in every rubric item. preference_following is included because a preference the conversation established is such a fact — of its 73 development rubric items a manner-of-writing screen confirmed 3 (results/analysis/beam-ability-taxonomy.json). instruction_following is excluded as a behavioural constraint rather than a locatable fact. That line is the owner's call, and it is a close one: the same screen puts instruction_following at 4 items of 68, so the two abilities are not separable by that measurement. Every alternative composition is therefore a fixed secondary below, reported whatever it says, so the choice can be audited against the result instead of trusted.

reported_separately.reason: instruction_following: the rubric grades whether a standing directive was obeyed — a behavioural constraint, not a fact that can be located in the conversation and traced through the pipeline. summarization: graded as coverage, 234 rubric items over 44 development questions, median 5 and up to 12, each a narrative span rather than a named fact, against an answerer whose prompt ends 'Answer directly and concisely' — answer length is the largest lever on it and length is not a memory property. Both are reported on every arm, never omitted.

secondary: mean rubric score over the 7 fact abilities alone
mean rubric score over the primary 8 (the registered headline)
mean rubric score over 9: the primary plus instruction_following
mean rubric score over all ten abilities
binary verdict (question mean >= 0.5) at each of those four compositions
a per-ability table of every metric above
analysis: paired sign-flip test over conversations on each conversation's mean difference
gate: none registered; a threshold may not be written against an unmeasured noise floor (results/gate-protocol.md). The development noise run measures run-to-run discordance, per-conversation spread and the intra-conversation correlation, and the gate is registered in an addendum after it.
noise_floor: unmeasured on BEAM; results/analysis/beam-power.json holds scenario estimates carried over from LongMemEval and the v4 probes

mandatory_secondary.name: evidence layers
mandatory_secondary.reason: A single source-recall number cannot separate four failures that call for four different fixes. `recall_stages.selected` is an any-session hit, so the 98.3% / 55% gap on LongMemEval could not be read as a reasoning-error rate. These four are reported on every arm of every run, fixed before any result exists.

layers.asks: did at least one labelled source session reach the context?
did every labelled source session reach it?
did the rubric's own required facts reach the final context?
of the required facts that did reach it, how many did the answer use?

separates: retrieved but dropped from the context
in the context and not used
mandatory_secondary.limits: The matcher decides an item only when it carries a distinctive token (money, percentage, written date, number with a unit from a closed list, multi-word proper noun). On the development half that is 261 of 1,165 rubric items (22%), and 191 of the 221 evidence-bearing ones (86%) are findable in their own labelled source — the instrument's ceiling. Both figures are reported beside any coverage number, and an undecidable item is never counted as a loss.
